The next logical step is to adjust the raycaster configuration in studio.js so that it doesn’t mistakenly intersect the thin edge outlines that are now part of the meshes (these outlines are rendered as line segments for visual detail). If the raycaster treats those lines as hits, selection will be flaky. 

I recall the current code in studio.js has:

```
this.raycaster = new THREE.Raycaster();
this.groundPlane = new THREE.Plane(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), 0);
```

There’s no special handling for line thresholds. To ignore the outlines, I should set `this.raycaster.params.Line.threshold` to a small value (e.g., 0.01). This will make line intersections require the cursor to be almost exactly on the line, effectively ignoring them for normal clicks. 

I need to edit studio.js, replacing the two‑line block with a three‑line block that adds the threshold setting. I’ll keep the existing raycaster and groundPlane initializations, just insert the new line in between. 

Thus the edit operation should target the exact snippet above, replace it with:

```
this.raycaster = new THREE.Raycaster();
this.raycaster.params.Line.threshold = 0.01; // ignore edge outlines
this.groundPlane = new THREE.Plane(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), 0);
```

This change directly addresses the raycast issue caused by the newly added edge outlines, aligns with the “studio raycast fix (meshes are now Groups)” note, and is a minimal, safe edit. I’ll now issue an Edit tool call with these parameters.
